image.title: G500-2023-General Motors
image.caption: Pre-owned General Motors Co. Chevrolet vehicles on a lot at the Green Chevrolet dealership in East Moline, Illinois, U.S., on Monday, May 3, 2021. General Motors Co. is scheduled to release earnings figures on May 5.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
The auto manufacturing giant led by Mary Barra jumped 14 spots on this year’s list.

  • Despite ongoing supply-chain issues and rising interest rates, GM brought in $9.9 billion in profits, down less than 1% from the year prior.

  • Barra has set ambitious goals for GM’s electric vehicle conversion, and the company has pledged to sell only zero-emissions vehicles by 2035. GM cut prices on its existing EV models in late 2022, and also introduced the Equinox, a $30,000 electric SUV.

  • GM is aiming to cut $2 billion in costs by the end of 2024. In early 2023, it initially avoided layoffs after 5,000 salaried workers took buyouts. The company later eliminated the jobs of several hundred contract workers.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: General Motors has gone further than many established auto manufacturers in the race to develop electric vehicles: GM says it will sell only zero-emissions vehicles by 2035. In January 2022 the company announced a $7 billion investment in the remodeling of several of its Michigan manufacturing facilities, with the aim of boosting EV pickup production. GM also announced that month that it would begin selling used cars on a new online platform called CarBravo.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Last year was a watershed for the auto industry from an investment perspective, as shares in incumbent carmakers came under pressure in the face of an mass investor exodus that favored upstart electric-vehicle manufacturers, especially Tesla. In August 2020, General Motors triggered the beginning of a rally in its stock price after unveiling its first serious Tesla competitor. The Cadillac Lyriq SUV will be built off a scalable architecture dedicated to battery-powered electric vehicles, an architecture designed to reduce costs and boost range. GM’s push into BEVs gained momentum following the November election. Days after President Biden took the U.S. back into the Paris Agreement in one of his first acts in office, CEO Mary Barra said her company would move to sell electric-only models exclusively by 2035—a dramatic shift for one of the giants of the automotive fossil-fuel era. As of mid-May 2021, GM’s stock had more than doubled since the Lyriq’s debut.

image.caption: SAO CAETANO DO SUL, BRAZIL - MAY 04: A technician of the General Motors factory repairs a ventilator from a public hospital amidst the COVID-19 pandemic on May 4, 2020 in Sao Caetano do Sul, Brazil.  A task force that includes the National Industrial Apprenticeship Service (SENAI), Ministry of Economy and ten major companies including General Motors, have teamed up to restore unused mechanical ventilators to help treat patients with COVID-19. So far, 500 units have been repaired. According to the Brazilian Health Ministry, there are 107,780 confirmed cases and at least 7,321 recorded deceases. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images)

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: A 40-day strike by General Motors workers at the company's U.S. factories left many Chevrolet and Cadillac dealers without inventory at the end of 2019. While consumers showed interest in the company’s midsize crossovers like the Chevrolet Equinox and Traverse, sales of larger SUVs such as the Cadillac Escalade and Chevrolet Suburban declined, contributing to a 16% slide in profits last year. Meanwhile customers just aren’t buying the well-reviewed Chevrolet Bolt electric vehicle.

companyRankingLists.description: Global business is back. After limping through a worldwide financial crisis and economic slowdown, the 500 largest companies ranked by revenues shattered all sorts of performance records in 2013: They racked up combined revenues of $31.1 trillion, up 2.5% from 2012, and profits soared 27% to nearly $2 trillion. China’s 95 companies (up from 89 last year) posted $5.8 trillion in revenues. The U.S. has four fewer companies on the list than last year but remains (for now) the country leader, with 128 corporations on the list—including No. 1 Wal-Mart Stores—reporting $8.6 trillion in revenues.
